direction: Warm character voices for a bright kid mystery game. Keep the delivery natural, gentle, and storybook-like.

clips.text: Kimmy Finch knows she was adopted, and her parents love her completely. Still, the first part of her story is a puzzle with only one clue: a tiny crescent locket. From her tree fort mystery club, Kimmy takes small cases around town. Today's case is bright, urgent, and very fluffy: find Pickles before the picnic begins.
Pickles slipped out while we were setting up for the picnic. She has a mint ribbon with a tiny bell, and she will do anything for carrot snacks. Start where snacks smell strongest.
I found flour paw prints near the patio chair, dear. A little cream rabbit sniffed the carrot rolls, then hopped toward the park. For a second I almost called you Mara. Silly old habit.

clips.voice: Mr. Basil Green, gentle older gardener
clips.text: A rabbit would choose the lavender bench if the picnic felt too noisy. Move slowly, offer a carrot top, then let her hear her little bell.
Carrot crumbs, a mint ribbon, and flour paw prints. Pickles was definitely here, and the trail points toward the park.
These paw prints are tiny and close together. Pickles was not running. She was exploring.
Quiet first, carrot second, bell last. We want Pickles to feel safe, not surprised.
The picnic envelope has a crescent-and-star mark like my locket. It might be nothing. Or it might belong in my other case file.
